fr.elements: Main Building; Vehicle Parking Area; Vehicle Parking Area; Internal Drive Aisle; Walkway; Landscaped Area; Roof Equipment
fr.considerations: Multiple Access Points; Limited Rear Access; Outdoor Storage
fr.recommendations:
• Mark all access points with address numbers visible from the street to help responders identify the correct entry during approach.
• Mark the rear access point with a visible building identifier so responders can confirm their position when approaching from that direction.
• Keep the rear access route clear of stored materials, equipment, and vehicles that would block emergency vehicle movement.
• Keep outdoor storage consolidated and away from building walls to allow responders to move around the structure without obstruction.
• Mark drive aisle directions and any dead ends to help responders navigate the site quickly under low-visibility conditions.
• Keep drive aisles clear of parked vehicles and stored materials to allow unobstructed emergency vehicle access to all sides of the building.
• Post a site map at the primary access point showing building entrances, the rear access route, and the location of any fixed roof equipment or utilities.

wildfire.conditions: Large Paved Area; Scattered Trees; Scattered Shrubs; Scattered Trees; Open Paved Area; Grass Cover; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Building; Adequate Vegetation Separation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim shrubs and low branches from trees located closest to the building where vegetation is growing near the structure.
• Remove dry or dead grass buildup from areas where grass cover is in contact with or near the building perimeter.
• Keep the large paved area and open paved areas clear of dead leaves, dry grass, and other loose plant material that can collect and ignite.
